I can't confirm that one, Riley. I don't give out quiz answers before a quiz is graded, and that includes confirming or ruling out a single option. "Just checking" counts the same way, because it would tell you the answer. This isn't about doubting you or your TA. If you want a TA-approved exception, ask them to tell me directly, or ask them to check the answer with you.

Here is a way to test your own pick, which works for any option on any item:

- Say in your own words what the model can and can't do on its own in this loop. For example, can it open a booking system? Can it run code?
- Then read each option and ask whether it describes something the model does, or something the surrounding program does.
- Put your reasoning for "a" in one sentence. If that sentence is about what the model itself outputs, and it holds up when you apply it to every option, you can trust it.

The agent loop is the idea the question is built on, and your learning record 0002 already shows you have it, so you have what you need to settle this yourself.

After quiz 0001 is graded, I'll go through q2 with you and show where each option goes wrong. Your NOTES also show you have two attempts on this quiz, so I can grade them once you tell me to.

Quick question to try now: in the makerspace assistant, which part of the system actually touches the booking calendar, the model or the program around it? Tell me what you think and why.
